section: How a foundation box is meant to drain
claim_or_recommendation: FAAC 770 N: operator protection class IP 67; installation includes a tube for draining rain water from the supporting box; motor cable joints inside the box need shunt boxes with protection class IP 67 or greater; inspect every six months; repairs only by qualified FAAC personnel and service centres.
qualification: Downloaded and read the official FAAC UK 770 N manual (732615 Rev.A): technical table (Protection class IP 67), section 4.3 step 5, section 4.6 step 2, sections 9 and 10. Supporting: older FAAC 770 manual https://www.faac.co.uk/productfiles/38_Manual_radC6CC0.pdf says to lay a second tube to drain rain water from the box to the nearest drain (not visibly linked; one FAAC link). Framed as one model-specific example; article says other models have their own arrangements. No claim about what IP 67 means beyond the manual's own wording.

claim_or_recommendation: After a flood: switch off at the consumer unit only if safe; do not attempt electrical repairs yourself; equipment affected by the flood must be professionally checked and tested; use a registered electrician; ask for an EICR.
qualification: Verified wording on the Electrical Safety First after-a-flood page on 22 October 2026 (HTTP 200). One visible ESF link. The page does not mention outdoor or gate equipment; the article applies it as general flood advice and says so.

claim_or_recommendation: Homeowner action stops at stopping use, keeping clear, switching off at a dry consumer unit if safe, photographs and calling an engineer. No lifting lids, pumping, bailing, vacuuming, drilling or sealing; no live-box intervention.
qualification: Original safety framework set by the editorial brief, consistent with ESF flood advice and the FAAC manual's repairs clause. Forum suggestions (drill a drain hole, silicone the cover, leave the lid open) cited as audience questions and explicitly discouraged.

claim_or_recommendation: Dangerous powered gates should be taken out of use until safety concerns are addressed; gates may drop or move unexpectedly during work if not adequately restrained.
qualification: Verified wording on the HSE powered gates basics page on 22 October 2026. One visible HSE link. Release position described with a hedge ("on many underground systems", "close to or under the box cover"); readers referred to their own system's instructions. FAAC 770 N user section confirms the release lever is part of the operator assembly in the box.

claim_or_recommendation: Around 4.5 million properties in England are in areas at risk of surface water flooding, about 1.1 million at high risk; the EA flood warning service does not cover surface water flooding because sudden rainstorms are hard to predict.
qualification: Read via the GOV.UK content API on 22 October 2026: section 5.4 (4.5 million, 1.1 million) and section 6.2 (warning service coverage). Published 30 June 2026. Table 2 (as of 31 March 2026) gives 4,547,600 and 1,014,100; rounded figures as the report states them. One visible gov.uk link.

claim_or_recommendation: Over one quarter of properties in areas at high flood risk from surface water flooding are in London; homeowners can check their postcode on the Check your long term flood risk service.
qualification: Supporting source, not visibly linked (one gov.uk link). Section 7.3 wording verified: over one quarter, nearly a third of a million (table: London 319,800, 29.9%). Service named without a link; https://check-long-term-flood-risk.service.gov.uk/ returns 301 to /postcode, checked 22 October 2026.
